portInfo.description: Almería’s Autoridad Portuaria manages passenger ferries and growing cruise traffic. The published Estación Marítima is an 8,400 m² two-floor building for regular North Africa ferry embarkation/disembarkation with ticket offices in public areas. APA news states a dedicated cruise passenger terminal will be completed in the first four months of 2027, following ~€2.8M of related investment already noted by APA president Rosario Soto in the same release. Cruise callers before that opening should expect existing passenger infrastructure and verify the day’s landing with sailing documents.

climate.description: Typical Mediterranean climate with seasonal variations

politics.visaRequirements: Entry and visa rules depend on nationality. Many visitors use Schengen short-stay rules, but requirements change—confirm with official government sources and your cruise line before travel.
politics.entryRequirements: Carry a valid passport (or a national ID where your cruise line and destination authorities accept it). Cruise transit formalities can differ from a normal airport entry—follow your ship’s document list.

gettingThere.distanceToCity: The Estación Marítima sits beside central Almería. Allow extra time in summer heat for the walk uphill to the Alcazaba.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: Add Cable Inglés and a longer lunch once your standard buffer is safe. Confirm whether your ship uses the ferry estación or a temporary cruise setup—the dedicated cruise terminal is not yet in service.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Ask whether you are using the ferry estación or a temporary cruise setup — APA’s dedicated terminal is due in the first four months of 2027.
